en.title: C continue Statement — Generalized Loop Output
en.description:
In the original code, s starts at 0 and is incremented in `while (s++ < 10)`; when s is less than both thresholds, the loop executes continue, otherwise it prints s. This site turns the upper limit and the two thresholds into inputs, keeping the loop and condition semantics unchanged.

The input protocol and the generalized ranges are additions by this site; they do not mean the original problem used stdin/stdout.
en.input: One line with three integers n, a, b. Ranges added by this site: 1≤n≤100000, 1≤a,b≤n.
en.output: Output every s that is not skipped by continue, in the order the original loop prints them, separated by spaces.
en.explanation: See the accompanying editorial for the approach, correctness, and complexity.
hints: Trace the state changes step by step; pay special attention to when the increment in the loop condition happens and to the execution order of finally.
